discussion_comments.comment_body:
Valid, and it went deeper than the bucketing. Fixed across 0caf11d and 17855b9.

0caf11d dropped the bucket and rebuilt `_relevance_rank_key`'s formula inside `_slot_key`. That closed the tie-break, but the two keys were still scoring **different text**: discovery computes `relevance` from the title alone (`reddit_rss.py:128`, `reddit_listing.py:114`) and `_relevance_rank_key` reads that stored value, while `_slot_key` recomputed over title + selftext. RSS carries up to 500 chars of selftext, so a post with a weak title and an on-topic body still won a slot and was still displayed last.

The reason I gave for recomputing (`post["relevance"]` not reliably set) was wrong — every path into `_slot_priority` runs through `reddit_rss` or `reddit_listing`, and both always set it. So 17855b9 calls the display key itself:

```python
def _slot_key(post):
    return (_payoff_tier(post), _relevance_rank_key(post))
```

Worth flagging: my first test for this passed against the recomputing version, because its fixtures had `selftext=""` and the divergence was invisible by construction. `test_slot_ranking_scores_the_same_text_as_display_ranking` fails against it; fixtures now fill `post["relevance"]` the way discovery does.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch, and it reproduced. I had assumed the new fallback was strictly tighter than the head check it replaces; it is not, the false-positive set moved. On the topic `AI code review bottleneck...`, an item titled "a barcode scanner written in rust" grounds under the fallback because `code` matches inside `barcode`, while the pre-fix `"ai" in haystack` check demoted it correctly. So this was a real regression on that class of item, not just residual looseness.

Tightening the way the comment implies does not work, though. Requiring *all* trailing tokens, or even two of them, fails the on-topic control test: a genuinely relevant item may legitimately name only `bottleneck`, and that test exists precisely to stop a fix that satisfies the demotion cases by grounding nothing.

What separates the two single-hit cases is that `bottleneck` matched as a word while `code` matched inside one. Fixed in 86e7b60 by anchoring the fallback to word starts. Prefix-anchored rather than fully word-bounded, so the inflection tolerance that matters is kept (`review` still grounds `reviewers`) while matches buried inside an unrelated word are dropped. The head branch is deliberately untouched, since its substring matching is load-bearing for brand compounds.

Added two regression tests: the `barcode` case from this comment, and one pinning the inflection tolerance so a future tightening cannot silently remove it. Verified the change flips only the intended case, and CI is green on the new head.

+# Generic tech terms that match too broadly to be the sole signal for a NARROW
+# topic ("cli" -> any CLI tool market; "ai" -> every AI market), but which ARE
+# the subject when the topic is a domain sweep rather than one product. Kept
+# separate from the rest of _NOISE_WORDS — the directional/sports/place words
+# there exist to PREVENT false matches ("NFC West" vs a "Kanye West" search),
+# so they must never be used as a positive signal.
+_DOMAIN_WORDS = frozenset({
+    "cli", "mcp", "protocol", "tool", "app", "code", "model", "ai", "api",
+    "software", "plugin", "skill", "agent", "bot", "search", "research",
+})
+
+# Soft residue left after stripping domain words from a sweep topic
+# ("AI frontier developments"). Domain-word fallback may fire when these are
+# the only informative leftovers. Distinctive terms like "benchmark" block it.
+_SWEEP_RESIDUE = frozenset({
+    "frontier", "developments", "development", "news", "trends", "trend",
+    "latest", "industry", "space", "ecosystem", "landscape", "overview",
+    "updates", "update", "future", "outlook", "sector", "field", "world",
+})
+
+_NOISE_WORDS = _NOISE_WORDS | _DOMAIN_WORDS
+
+
+def _domain_word_fallback_allows(core_words: list[str], informative: list[str],
+                                 title_lower: str, title_words: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Allow domain-word title matches only for pure/soft domain sweeps.
+
+    Blocks mixed topics like \"MCP protocol benchmark\" from accepting a Kyoto
+    Protocol market via the shared domain token \"protocol\" when the distinctive
+    informative word (\"benchmark\") missed.
+    """
+    hard_informative = [w for w in informative if w not in _SWEEP_RESIDUE]

> The tighter bucket is based only on the requested span, but Reddit anchors that bucket to the current time rather than `to_date`.

Fixed in a21c463 — bucket selection now takes `max(span, age_of_from_date)` (with one day of rolling/calendar slack), so a one-day request ending two weeks ago picks `month` and still reaches `from_date`. Covered by `test_window_to_time_filter_covers_historical_from_date`.
